content:
Alex: Heads-up — saw a memory growth pattern in prod replicas handling long chats (>65k tokens). Not a leak per-se, looks like KV cache fragmentation + lots of small allocations piling up. Attach a quick profile later.
Maya: Ugh. Is this the same stack that regressed after the quantize change last week? :grimacing:
Alex: Possibly related. perf-bot reported a 6% P99 increase and memory drift on the r3 pool after we switched to mixed-quant kernels.
perf-bot: [alert] perf/regression: r3-longcontext P99 +6% over baseline; mem-resident +14% after 2024-11-09 deploy.
Chen: Any flamegraphs or heap snapshots? Fragmentation hints are best with allocation histograms.
Alex: Will paste the short bits. Main observation: large number of tiny KV blocks (~1-4KB) allocated from the slab allocator, but free map shows many holes >8KB that aren't coalescing. Allocation pattern seems to be: long-prefix cache entries -> incremental updates -> small rewrites.
Alex: sample log lines:
```
KVPool: alloc id=0x7f3a size=3072 from bucket=4
KVPool: free id=0x7f2b size=4096 -> mark-stale
KVPool: alloc id=0x7f5c size=2048 from bucket=2
KVPool: scan-compaction: skipped region 0x1000-0x1fff, fragmented
```
Maya: So buddy coalesce isn't triggering, or buddy sizes don't match our churn. We tuned buckets to powers-of-two earlier which might amplify internal fragmentation for many small updates.
Dmitri: Also worth checking interaction with batching — when we coalesce KV caches across requests (for batching), we get temporary spikes of heterogenous sizes. Kernel selection change for quantized kernels may alter avg seq lengths and thus chunk sizes.
Sam: I ran a local stim test reproducer: using convo-generator with 80k context and jittered update writes. I can share the harness. It shows high count of free segments but low contiguous space.
Chen: Proposal: two-pronged approach: (1) microcompactor that does best-effort compaction of adjacent free blocks during idle cycles (non-blocking), (2) tune bucket strategy to include mixed-size bins (e.g., 2KB,3KB,6KB,12KB) instead of pure POW2 to reduce leftover slop for typical update sizes.
Maya: Microcompactor needs to be safe for concurrent reads — prefer copy-on-write moving with short-held locks, or do it only for cold KV entries.
Alex: Another idea: per-model bucket bias. Models with long-context routing (chat-long) get larger base chunk-size to reduce fragmentation. Light models keep small buckets. Router knows model tag.
Dmitri: That ties into smart routing: route long-context to pools pre-tuned with larger slab sizes/kernels to reduce fragmentation *and* kernel mismatch. Might be bigger infra change but elegant.
Sam: I tried a quick patch to allocator that delayed freeing small segments into a staging buffer for 100ms and then attempted coalesce — reduced fragmentation in the reproducer by ~35%. But it's a hack.
Chen: Nice quick win. But staging increases transient resident mem. Need SLO tradeoff.
Alex: For testing: 1) run reproducer across r3 and r4 kernels (quantized vs fp16) to decouple kernel selection impact; 2) try the staging/coalesce patch; 3) run mixed-bucket allocator sim for 24h on simulated churn.
perf-bot: Suggested benchmark: /bench/kv-longcontext/auto-100k/10k-reqs with metrics: P99 latency, RSS, fragmentation-ratio.
Maya: I can own the mixed-bucket sim and microcompactor design doc. Will sketch API: `compact_scan(max_bytes, max_time_ms)` and `bucket_profile(model_tag)`.
Dmitri: I'll instrument kernel-selection path to log sequence-length histograms and batch-size distribution so we can correlate changes to allocation sizes.
Alex: Sam, can you run the staging/coalesce patch on a canary pool tomorrow and collect heap histograms?
Sam: Yep. I'll run it on canary-5 between 02:00-04:00 PST and post results.
Chen: If microcompactor looks promising, we should gate it behind a flag and enable for long-context pools only. Also add metrics: compactions_attempted, compactions_bytes_moved, compaction_time_ms.
Maya: Agreed. Also add an eviction-heuristic tweak: prefer evicting cold small segments that would unblock large region coalesces first. That way eviction creates useful contiguous free space.
Alex: Good point — eviction policy can help defragmentation indirectly. Let's avoid global stop-the-world compaction.
Dmitri: One more thought: try variable-size slab arenas where a long-context arena uses larger page sizes so buddy coalescing uses fewer pieces. OS/pagemap implications but could help.
Sam: After my canary run I'll post the heap diffs and a small patch to the allocator to show the delta.
Alex: OK team — plan: Maya doc + sim, Sam canary test, Dmitri hist instrumentation, Chen compaction metrics. We'll reconvene after results. Thanks. :thumbsup:
